accepted.evidence: Dhakal pp. 65 and 68 prints /cʰə/ six. Turner section 3 has Prakrit cha and Nepali cha from *kṣaṭ, contrasting section 1 ṣa/ṣe-type forms and section 2 ṣu-type forms. The house transcription cʰ→ʦʰ is retained; both source examples share this lexical numeral.

Dhakal pp. 65 and 68 prints /cʰə/ six. Turner section 3 has Prakrit cha and Nepali cha from *kṣaṭ, contrasting section 1 ṣa/ṣe-type forms and section 2 ṣu-type forms. The house transcription cʰ→ʦʰ is retained; both source examples share this lexical numeral.

Dhakal pp. 53 and 68 explicitly gives /hẽṭʰ/ below/down with final aspirated retroflex. Turner section 2 gives Pali/Pk heṭṭhā, Punjabi heṭh and Bhojpuri heṭhā̃ under *adhiṣṭāt. The source nasalization is preserved, and section 1 adhastāt is not selected.

Dhakal p. 62 prints /bəl.wa/ sand. Turner11580 gives Prakrit vāluā and Nepali bāluwā/baluwā, matching the b-l-w sequence and sense. Darai vowel length is noncontrastive (p. 42); the first vowel and contracted middle syllable remain as printed.

Dhakal p. 59 explicitly labels /ek.ṭa/ one-CLF. The earlier linked Darai ek is the base; -ṭa is a source-attested classifier, so this is a synchronic derived link to the same-source lexical numeral rather than a direct reflex of the whole form.
